brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.requirement: Holder for the soldering iron while switched on and hot
requirements.evidence: Cell 1,0,0 carries bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full left empty as a dedicated rest for the hot iron, separated from the other two cells so the hot tip is isolated. No heat-resistant iron stand exists in the Hex Cluster catalog; the bin is 3D-printed plastic and the configurator does not verify heat/temperature resistance, so a printed part must not be treated as safe for a hot iron without a bought metal stand placed in it.

requirements.requirement: Two bins for solder and spare tips
requirements.evidence: bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) staged with solder-reel in one compartment and heap-standoffs-div3 as stand-in for spare tips in the other compartment; bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full provides second full-depth storage volume for bulk solder/tips. Build has 3 bins total, satisfying the two-bin requirement.

finish.summary: Three-cell linear bench station: one isolated empty full-depth bin as the hot-iron parking position, and two storage volumes (one divided 2-compartment bin + one full bin) for solder and spare tips. Staged with solder reel and tips props. Capped open faces and locked joints. Iron holder is shape-only - no catalog part is rated for hot-iron contact; user must add a metal iron stand.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
